title: What a Law Is
objective: After this level you can explain what makes a rule a law.
summary: A law is a rule a community recognizes as binding, enforced by a controlling authority. Around 1750 BCE, Hammurabi of Babylon set 282 rulings in stone, written as if-then laws.

cards.headline: About 3,800 years ago, a king had his laws carved into stone.
cards.body: Around 1750 BCE, Hammurabi of Babylon had 282 legal rulings engraved on a black stone slab more than 2.25 meters tall. You can see it today in the Louvre in Paris. Why go to all that trouble? Because it shows what turns a rule into a law.

cards.headline: Rules versus laws
cards.body: Your household might ban shoes indoors. That's a rule, but not a law. Britannica describes law as the rules of conduct that a community recognizes as binding, enforced through a controlling authority. Two things make the difference: the whole community is bound by it, and an authority (Level 3's accepted power) stands ready to enforce it.

cards.headline: If this, then that
cards.body: Hammurabi's laws follow one pattern: if someone does this, then that follows. Law 196 is the famous one: if a man puts out another man's eye, his eye shall be put out. An eye for an eye. Every law is a consequence spelled out in advance, not made up after the fact.

cards.fact: The code invited wronged people to come and read it.
cards.context: Its closing words tell anyone oppressed who has a case at law to stand before the king's image and read the inscription. A law everyone can read is a law everyone can point to. Equal for all, though? Not quite. Penalties varied with the offender's social status.

mascot.line: Written down, public and enforced: a big step. Fair to everyone: a later chapter's story.

cards.headline: Law: laid down
learned: A law binds a whole community

questions.prompt: What did Hammurabi's great stone slab record?

options.label: A map of Babylon's canals
options.rationale: It holds laws, not a map.

options.label: A list of Babylon's kings
options.rationale: It's a law code, not a king list.

options.label: The city's tax receipts
options.rationale: It records legal rulings, not receipts.

questions.explanation: Around 1750 BCE, Hammurabi had 282 legal rulings engraved on a black stone stela, now in the Louvre.

questions.prompt: Why is a family's "no shoes indoors" rule not a law?

options.label: No controlling authority enforces it on a whole community
It was never carved into a stone slab like Hammurabi's
options.rationale: Laws don't need stone; they need community recognition and enforcement.

options.label: It isn't written in if-then form like a real law
Only kings and queens are allowed to make rules
options.rationale: Kings aren't required; a controlling authority is.

questions.explanation: Law is the set of rules a community recognizes as binding, enforced through a controlling authority.

questions.prompt: Level 3 defined authority as accepted power. What role does it play in making a law?

options.label: It carves the law into stone
options.rationale: Carving was Hammurabi's choice, not what makes a law.

options.label: It decides which games people play
options.rationale: That's closer to Level 2's football rules.

options.label: It stands behind the rule and enforces it
It makes the law apply only to rulers
options.rationale: Laws bind the community, not only rulers.

questions.explanation: A law is enforced through a controlling authority: accepted power standing behind the rule.
